correctness.rationale: For each t>0, spectral calculus reduces the complementary exponential to an order interval between aQ and bQ. The entrywise optimization of a symmetric rank-two form has exact eigenvalues (c±αβ)/2; choosing rank-one spectral projections gives both attained bounds with a single generator independent of t. The derived positivity condition is H(t)>=R, and direct differentiation proves H increases strictly from (L+δ)/(L-δ) to infinity. Sharpness is witnessed by one three-level generator for all earlier positive times. Diagonal entries are strictly positive by positive definiteness. Rational identities and 14617 finite diagnostic assertions passed; computations are not the infinite/universal proof.

value.rationale: The uniform positivity time is a natural, computable semigroup invariant when only spectral gap/window and Perron eigenvector are prescribed. The result gives both sharp upper and lower entrywise bounds, an exact universal threshold using the two most imbalanced coordinates, an explicit closed case for equally spaced spectral levels, and a single all-earlier-times counterexample. This strengthens qualitative eventual positivity with an attained necessary-and-sufficient design guarantee; it is not a table recomputation or routine substitution.
